'''Alan Davison'''  [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]]<ref name=frs>{{cite journal|last1=Green|first1=Malcolm L. H.|author-link1=Malcolm Green (chemist)|last2=Cummins|first2=Christopher C.|last3=Kronauge|first3=James F.|title=Alan Davison. 24 March 1936 — 14 November 2015|journal=[[Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society]]|year=2017|volume=63|pages=197–213|issn=0080-4606|doi=10.1098/rsbm.2017.0004|doi-access=free}}</ref> (24 March 1936 — 14 November 2015) was a British inorganic chemist known for his work on transition metals, and a professor at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://mit.edu/chemistry/www/faculty/davison.html |title=Alan Davison, Professor of Chemistry |website=mit.edu |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120202120128/http://mit.edu/chemistry/www/faculty/davison.html |archive-date=2012-02-02 }}</ref>

==Education==
He earned a B.Sc. from [[Swansea University]] in 1959, and Ph.D. from [[Imperial College London]] in 1962,<ref>{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|publisher=Imperial College London|title=Studies on the chemistry of transition metal carbonyls|first= Alan|last=Davison|date=1962|url=http://ethos.bl.uk/OrderDetails.do?uin=uk.bl.ethos.602048|website=ethos.bl.uk|hdl=10044/1/13205}}</ref>  supervised by Nobel Laureate Sir [[Geoffrey Wilkinson]].<ref name=mitdv/>

==Career and research==
Davison discovered the radioactive heart imaging agent Cardiolite, [[Technetium (99mTc) sestamibi]].<ref>{{cite book|first=Abhik |last=Ghosh |title=Letters to a Young Chemist |publisher=Wiley-Interscience |year=2011 |pages=134–135 |isbn=978-0-470-39043-6}}</ref>

===Awards and honours===
He was recipient of the following:<ref name=mitdv>{{cite web|title=Wallace H. Carothers Award Lecture – Professor Alan Davison, MIT |url=http://www.mitdv.org/events/archives/2006/04/wallace_h_carot_1.html |date=4 April 2006 |website=mitdv.org}}</ref>
* [[Alfred P. Sloan Foundation]] [[Fellow]] (1967)<ref name="MIT obituary"/>
* Paul C. Aebersold Award for Outstanding Achievement in Basic Science Applied to Nuclear Medicine (1993)<ref name=SNMMI>{{cite web|work=[[SNMMI]] |title=Paul C. Aebersold Award Recipients |url=http://www.snmmi.org/AboutSNMMI/Content.aspx?ItemNumber=5110 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924042922/http://www.snmmi.org/AboutSNMMI/Content.aspx?ItemNumber=5110 |archive-date=24 September 2015 |access-date=10 October 2018}}</ref>
* Ernest H. Swift Lectureship at the [[California Institute of Technology]] (1999)<ref name="MIT obituary"/>
* Fellow of the [[Royal Society]] of London (2000)<ref name=frs/>
* [[American Chemical Society]] Award for Creative Invention (2006)<ref name="MIT obituary"/>
* Gabbay Award (2006)<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.brandeis.edu/rosenstiel/gabbayaward/past.html|title=Gabbay Award Winners: 9th (2006) |publisher=[[Brandeis University]] |website=brandeis.edu}}</ref>
* Carothers Award for outstanding contributions and advances in industrial applications of Chemistry (2006)<ref name="MIT obituary"/>
* [[George Charles de Hevesy]] Nuclear Pioneer Award (2009)<ref>{{cite web|work=[[SNMMI]] |title=de Hevesy Award Recipients |url=https://www.snmmi.org/AboutSNMMI/Content.aspx?ItemNumber=33878 |access-date=7 November 2023}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Davison died after a long illness on 14 November 2015 at the age of 79.<ref name=frs/><ref name="MIT obituary">{{cite web|url=https://news.mit.edu/2015/chemistry-professor-emeritus-alan-davison-dies-1117 |title=Alan Davison, professor emeritus of chemistry, dies at 79 |work=MIT News |date=17 November 2015 |last=McGrath |first=Liz}}</ref>

==In popular culture==

In an episode of [[Friday Night Dinner]], family patriarch and chemistry enthusiast Martin Goodman mishears the name "Alison" as "Alan Davison".{{cn|date=November 2023}}
